brief.headline: Three linked concerns this period: new evening confusion with a stove-safety event, 8.4% weight loss in about 12 weeks, and three elevated BP readings with missed evening doses.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 the RN documented about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. She was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. The PCP note of 2026-11-03 says only that chronic conditions are stable. The notes provided show no urinalysis result or medication review outcome, and no later cognition follow-up.
items.verifier_note: The 10-26 RN note matches every clinical detail. The 11-03 PCP note says only that chronic conditions are stable. Neither note has a urinalysis result, a medication review outcome, or a cognition follow-up.

items.statement: Weight fell from 68.9 kg on 2026-09-05 to 63.1 kg on 2026-11-24, a loss of 5.8 kg (8.4%). Readings were 66.9 kg on 10-01 and 64.8 kg on 10-28. On 11-24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record has all four weights and the -5.8 kg (-8.4%) change. The dietitian note supports the poor appetite, skipped breakfast, 50% of lunches eaten, and the plan.

items.statement: BP was above the 140/90 threshold on all three readings in the period: 167/92 on 10-04, 172/92 on 10-25 and 163/96 on 11-15. On 11-15 Luisa admitted missing evening doses some days, and the RN flagged the regimen for PCP review. The medication record shows no changes since 2026-09-01, and the PCP note of 11-03 does not mention BP.
items.verifier_note: The three BP readings and the 140/90 threshold match the vitals record. The 11-15 RN note supports the missed evening doses and the PCP review flag. The medication record shows nothing started or stopped. The 11-03 PCP note does not mention BP.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window: ED visits, urgent care, admissions, observation stays, and readmissions, with reasons and discharge summaries.
Falls and near-falls: count and document any falls, injuries, or fall-risk screens, especially given antihypertensives (amlodipine, metoprolol), nitroglycerin use, and diphenhydramine.

Cardiac symptoms: review chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin PRN use frequency, dyspnea, palpitations, and any cardiology visits or ECG/troponin results, given ischemic heart disease on clopidogrel, metoprolol, and simvastatin.
Bleeding and anemia: review any bleeding events, bruising, GI bleeding signs, and recent CBC/hemoglobin trend, since she is on clopidogrel and has a documented anemia diagnosis.
Blood pressure trend: pull all BP readings in the window, check for hypotension or orthostatic symptoms after the amlodipine start (2026-02-18), and flag readings above or below the team's targets.

Diabetes and glycemic control: review HbA1c, fasting and random glucose, hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia events, and metformin tolerance (GI symptoms, renal function/eGFR, B12 level given long-term metformin use and the B12 injection), and confirm the metformin start date of 2026-02-18 against the record.

Lipids: review most recent lipid panel including triglycerides (hypertriglyceridemia on record) and assess simvastatin 20 mg adherence and whether the dose still matches current lipid results and cardiac risk.
Weight and BMI trend: compare weights across the window against the obesity/metabolic syndrome history; flag gain or loss of 5% or more.

Medication reconciliation: compare the active list against the pharmacy fill history and the start/stop log for the window; confirm no new starts or stops occurred beyond the 2026-02-18 changes; review diphenhydramine (anticholinergic, from 1961) for appropriateness and cognitive/fall risk; review allergy list (shellfish, wheat, soy, mold, animal dander, grass and tree pollen) against any new prescriptions or supplements.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: review ADL/IADL changes, cognitive screen results, depression screen (PHQ-type), social isolation or attendance at PACE day center and missed visits, caregiver or home-situation changes, and any care-plan goals or assessments due in the window (for example, reassessment or care plan review date falling by 2026-11-30).

trace.headline: Luisa has new evening confusion with a stove-safety event, an 8.4% weight loss since Sep 5, and three elevated BP readings with missed evening doses. The evidence doesn't show a documented follow-up on the confusion.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 the RN recorded that Maria reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. Luisa was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. Plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week.

The evidence has no urinalysis result or medication review outcome. The PCP progress note of 2026-11-03 says chronic conditions are stable and doesn't mention the confusion. No encounters are recorded in the period.
Weight fell from 68.9 kg (2026-09-05) to 66.9 (10-01), 64.8 (10-28) and 63.1 kg (11-24). That is a 5.8 kg (12.8 lb, 8.4%) loss over about 11 weeks, with a steady decline at each reading.

On 2026-11-24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfast, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. Plan is an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems.

BP was above the 140/90 threshold on all three readings in the period: 167/92 (2026-10-04), 172/92 (10-25) and 163/96 (11-15). On 11-15 Luisa admitted missing evening doses some days, and the RN flagged the antihypertensive regimen for PCP review.

Amlodipine 2.5 mg (started 2026-02-18) is the only new antihypertensive on the medication list, and no medication changes are recorded in the period. The PCP note of 2026-11-03 says to continue the current plan, and the elevated BP and missed doses are not addressed in the evidence.

Diphenhydramine 25 mg is on the active medication list while evening confusion is being worked up. The medication review planned on 2026-10-26 should cover the full list. The evidence doesn't show how often she takes it.
No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 2026-08-01. The last dose was 2026-02-18.
